title: GraphMemix — paper view
subtitle: The mechanism as Li et al. describe it. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); A3 ADMIT, A6 and B8 are empty — the paper defines no such step.
source: Li et al. 2026, GraphMemix (arXiv:2608.26983v1, MemoraX AI Research)   ·   verified against servers/graphmemix/verification.md (34 paper-side assertions: 24 ✓ / 3 ✗ / 7 ◐ / 0 ?)
legend_notes: A3 ADMIT is entirely empty by design: no dedup, no conflict resolution, no eviction anywhere in the pipeline. The paper puts its whole methodological bet on B4-B5 (node verifier + edge verifier + exact forest optimization) instead — the inverse of the MIRIX/SGM/A-MEM write-time-consolidation family it argues against (§1, §2.1).

B5 SELECT is a genuine 'solve exactly' pipeline: Kruskal computes the maximum-weight forest exactly at every step of the 1-swap local search (fixed cardinality K=10), then a second bounded-exact stage enumerates every nonempty subset of that proposal to guarantee a global optimum within it (Eq.13).

The paper's implicit 'no generative LLM at write time' framing does not hold universally: H2HMem's 1,300 images get a one-time LLM-generated caption sidecar (Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, A.1) before indexing — the one dataset where write-time pays a generation cost.

Node verifier and ECV are drawn as two distinct primitives on purpose: the verifier scores individual candidates (P-RERANK), ECV scores (anchor, candidate) EDGES with a six-way role gate (P-EDGEVERIFY) and produces a trusted edge set G_q^trust, not a re-ranked list. Merging them would erase the redundancy/conflict semantics the forest solver depends on.
